limits: THE RUNNER-LANE HALF, and the first control in this repository to exercise a gate path that reaches `lib.cicd`. That was impossible until issue #1163: `lib/cicd/__init__.py` re-exported sixteen submodules eagerly, two of them importing pydantic, so `python3 -m lib.cicd` could not start in the negative-controls image - measured four ways before the change. The re-exports are deferred now and the derivation runs on the stdlib alone. Verified as the WHOLE control under the pinned image digest with `--network none` and a read-only workspace. WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that subsumption is DERIVED from the aggregate's own prerequisite list rather than assumed from the presence of a `verify:` target. The bad case's `verify:` names test and typecheck and NOT lint, and lint is broken: the gate must still run lint and red. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that a derived prerequisite is one make would actually RUN - an inactive `ifeq` rule and a step whose configured command differs from `make <target>` are both still read as coverage (issue #1165) - nor anything about the `not-run` accounting, which is `controls/flow-finish-gate-subsumption`'s subject. SEPARATE FROM THAT SIBLING ON MEASUREMENT, not preference: `check-negative-controls.py` runs EVERY anchor against EVERY bad case and requires each to miss, and the sibling's 529d470 anchor already carries #1152's derivation, so it CATCHES this case and would score it INERT. The same split, for the same reason, as `controls/flow-finish-gate-plan-reconciliation`. TWO STUBS, EACH STANDING IN FOR AN ENVIRONMENT AND NOTHING ELSE: `bin/make`, because make is absent from the image, with the Makefile beside it real text that the derivation actually reads; and `bin/uv`, which resolves `uv run --project <CPP> python -m lib.cicd` to the interpreter already present. The module that executes is the repository's own, so the derivation under test is the shipped one rather than a re-description of it. SINCE #1165 THE DERIVATION ASKS MAKE (`make -p -n`) RATHER THAN READING THE MAKEFILE, and three cases cover what that buys. `bad-inactive-conditional-prereq` puts `verify: lint` inside `ifeq (1,0)`: a textual reader reports lint as a prerequisite, subsumption marks it covered, `make verify` runs without it, and a BROKEN LINT passes as a `subsumed` gate - measured on the pre-fix derivation as `SUBSUMED: lint, test, typecheck` followed by `FLOW_FINISH_GATE: ok`. COMMAND-EQUIVALENCE IS NOT COVERED BY A CASE HERE, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. A `bad-step-command-mismatch` case shipped in an earlier revision of this branch and was WITHDRAWN when a counter-model review (round 2) showed it detected through an unrelated failure: it configured the mismatch through `.claude/cicd_tasks.yml`, the manifest reader needs pydantic, and the battery image deliberately has none (#1163) - so plan resolution raised before subsumption ran, the gate reported `fail`, and the case's detect_signal was satisfied by an import error. Deleting the command check entirely would not have changed its verdict. Isolating the property needs a step whose command is not `make <id>` while its ENVIRONMENT matches the aggregate's, and the built-in finish plan contains no such step: lint, test and typecheck all resolve to a recognised `make` invocation, and `security_scan` differs in both, so the environment refusal fires first and the command refusal is never the reason. Configuring one requires a manifest, which requires pydantic, which the image refuses by design - so the property is covered by unit tests (tests/test_runner.py::TestSubsumedGates) and NOT by a registered control. A case that detects for the wrong reason is worse than a named gap: it reports coverage that does not exist. `good-make-absent` is the SAFETY PROPERTY and is why the other two are safe to ship: its `make` runs targets but refuses `-p`, so the derivation cannot be answered, NOTHING is subsumed, and all four gates run - the direction this fix must fail in, because the alternative is the textual fall-back the issue is about. `bad-make-absent-textual-fallback` IS THE HALF `good-make-absent` CANNOT MEASURE (counter-model review): every gate passes in that case, so a derivation that fell back to reading the Makefile - subsuming lint, test and typecheck and running only `verify` - would exit 0 there too, and the case would stay green while the property it names had been lost. This case is the same `-p`-refusing make over a BROKEN lint, which separates them in the verdict: nothing subsumed runs `make lint` on its own and reds, while a textual fall-back runs only `verify`, whose recipe does not run its prerequisites, and greens. The good case says the fall-back direction is SAFE; only this one says it is what happened. SINCE OPTION B THE QUESTION IS ASKED ONE STEP EARLIER, and `bad-inactive-conditional-prereq` now reds for a STRONGER reason than it did when this control was written. Two counter-model passes produced fifteen findings against a derivation that read make's answer - inactive conditionals, MAKECMDGOALS, MAKEFLAGS, recursive $(MAKE), target-specific variables, escaped hashes, escaped spaces - every one of them a gate recorded as covered while never running, and every one a construct nobody had listed. So the makefile must now be POSITIVELY inside a small closed grammar (plain rules, tab recipes, plain assignments with no $(shell)/$(eval)/$(MAKE)/MAKEFLAGS in the value, .PHONY) BEFORE make is asked at all; anything else refuses by construction, names the line and the construct, and every gate runs. That case's `ifeq` is outside the set, so it is refused before `make -p -n` executes rather than after its answer is parsed - which also means the query never runs a recursive make or a MAKEFLAGS-sensitive conditional. `good-all-listed` is INSIDE the grammar and therefore still exercises real subsumption rather than the refusal path; that is deliberate, since a control in which every case refuses would prove only that refusing works. THE CASES NO LONGER STUB `make` (except that one, which stubs it to model one variable): they need a REAL make, which `scripts/ci-stage-make.py` now stages into `.ci-bin` for the battery step, because the image has none and without it this control measures make's ABSENCE instead of its subject. ISOLATION (attachment coupling, 2026-09-22): cases run through the shared runner controls/flow-finish-gate/run-case.sh, which copies the case outside every git repository before running the gate. They previously ran IN PLACE inside this checkout, so the gate read the ENCLOSING repository's git state - a fact the fixture never chose - looked for a counter-model receipt on that branch, found none, and this control's GOOD case failed. Measured at one sha: attached to a branch -> fail, DETACHED at the same sha -> ok, attached to main -> fail. ATTACHMENT is the variable, so main fails permanently and CI, always detached, can never see it. Only GOOD cases were contaminated: a failing gate step short-circuits before the counter-model check, so every BAD case redded correctly in place. NO detect_signal CHANGED in that work - the anchor causes none of these failures and -derivation is anchored AND passed both ways, which refutes it as the cause.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED because no historical article carries this defect: no released gate deduplicated gates at all before #1152, so none of them can be blind to a bad derivation. What it reproduces is the obvious WRONG FIX - treat the presence of a `verify:` target as covering lint, test and typecheck instead of deriving which of them it names. Deliberately not the real gate with one line changed: the real gate reaches its verdict through the Python runner, and an anchor carrying all of that would measure the harness rather than the decision. Measured on both cases: it prints `FLOW_FINISH_GATE: ok` and exits 0 on the known-bad input - it runs `make verify`, which succeeds precisely because it never runs the broken lint - and it agrees with the fixed gate on the known-good one.
